subject: SCIENCE
title: Family Traits
objective: Compare inherited traits using fictional organisms.
introduction: Milo compares fictional young organisms with their parents. Which traits can be inherited, and why are young ones not exact copies?

vocabulary.definition: Everything around a living thing, including land, water, air, and other organisms.
A feature of a living thing, such as color, shape, or fur pattern.
A living thing that grows, uses energy, and can respond.

activities.instruction: Watch Milo compare inherited traits in fictional organisms.
activities.content: Offspring can inherit traits but are not exact copies; traits can involve genes and environment.

feedback.retry: Check whether the trait is present from birth and can resemble a parent’s trait.

activities.accessibilityAlternative: Text alternative: Offspring can inherit traits but are not exact copies; traits can involve genes and environment.

activities.instruction: Tap each fictional organism and notice the trait it shares.

examples: a beetle shares a color pattern with its parent
an imaginary plant has a leaf shape like its parent
a cartoon animal has a fur pattern like its parent

feedback.correct: Great! You found the examples for Family Traits. 🔎
feedback.retry: For each organism, name the trait and compare it with the fictional parent.

activities.accessibilityAlternative: A numbered list of the same examples is available for keyboard and screen-reader use.

options: Offspring may resemble parents without being exact copies.

feedback.correct: Correct: Offspring may resemble parents without being exact copies.

items.prompt: Milo compares fictional young organisms with their parents. Which statement about inherited traits is true?

options.text: Offspring can inherit traits but are not exact copies; genes and environment can both matter.
Young organisms inherit every learned habit.

items.explanation: Young organisms can inherit traits and still differ from their parents. Genes influence traits, and the environment can shape how some traits appear.

items.prompt: A fictional beetle is born with a color pattern like its parent. Which trait could be inherited?
items.explanation: A color pattern present from birth can be inherited from parents. A haircut, scar, or learned song happens after birth.

items.prompt: Milo writes four claims about offspring. Which one is NOT true?

options.text: Young ones can be born with traits from parents
Traits can be shaped by the environment
Offspring are always exact copies of one parent
Each young organism can have its own combination of traits

items.explanation: Young organisms can resemble parents without being exact copies. Each one has its own combination, and the environment can affect some traits.

items.prompt: Maxine compares a fictional parent and young organism. Which statement is true?

options.text: Offspring may resemble parents without being exact copies.
Young organisms have no traits at birth.

items.explanation: A young organism may share traits with a parent while still being different. Inherited traits are present early, and the environment can also influence some features.

items.prompt: A cartoon animal is born with a fur pattern like its parent. Which trait could be inherited?

options.text: A scar from a later fall

items.explanation: A fur pattern present from birth can come from parents. A learned song, toy, or later scar is not inherited in that way.
